title: Metering and Tiers Playbook: Token Pricing & Discount Guidance
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is meant for go-to-market, sales, and product partners to align on metric framing for metering, the rationale for token pricing, proposed tier constructs, and guardrails for discounting and negotiations. It reflects product constraints (hosted, dedicated, private) and how pricing signals should map to value for developers, platform teams, and enterprises.

High-level positioning thesis:
- Charge for what customers scale: tokens are a direct proxy for compute, model usage, and predictable unit economics across generation and embeddings.
- Keep billing simple and signal fairness: one metered unit enables predictable consumption modeling across clients, avoids meter proliferation, and aligns with how customers architect prompts.
- Provide clear enterprise levers: reserved capacity, committed spend discounts, and private deployment licensing separate infrastructure/value components from per-token marginal usage.

Why token pricing (short bullets for comms):
- Directly correlates to cost drivers (tokens -> GPU cycles -> cost).
- Familiar to customers using LLM APIs; easier to model ROI for features (e.g., chat session tokens).
- Works across model types and is model-agnostic (we can apply weightings where appropriate).
- Allows consistent bundling (free tiers, trial quotas, monthly credits).

Competitive snapshot (how to talk about competitors):
- Cloud AI managed endpoints: tend to meter by instance-hours or vCPU/GPU-hours. Position: those work for heavy custom infra but are opaque for product usage and harder to map to feature-level economics.
- LLM API providers: many already use token pricing; we differentiate by predictable SLAs (Dedicated), private offerings, and tooling that reduces unit cost (Optimize).
- Inference infra vendors: typically sell fixed licenses or appliance pricing. Position: good for ops teams but lacks flexible consumption. Our hybrid (tokens + reserved capacity) offers both predictability and elasticity.

Tier architecture proposal (naming + what to include):
- Developer (Free): 100k free tokens / month, community models, basic rate limits, access to SDK and console. Purpose: lower barrier to try, PLG funnel.
- Growth: metered token price (base rate), access to curated faster models, higher rate limits, per-project analytics, email support.
- Business: lower per-token price, access to Dedicated burst, priority support, per-route dashboards, basic rollout controls and evaluation tooling.
- Enterprise: custom per-token pricing or hybrid (commit + reduced metered rate), Dedicated clusters or Private deployment, SSO/KMS, longer retention for observability, enterprise SLAs and white-glove onboarding.

Examples for internal use (sample numbers — for illustration only):
- Growth: $0.0008 / token for generation; $0.0005 / token for embeddings. 1M tokens -> $800 generation cost pre-discount.
- Business: 20% discount applied to Growth list for annual prepay of $50k.
- Enterprise: committed capacity contract: $X/month for N GPUs + unit token price of $0.0003 beyond commit.

Metering rules (important operational details to be explicit about):
- Token definition: tokens counted as the sequence tokens sent + sequence tokens returned for generations; embeddings are measured by input tokenization only.
- Rounding and billing windows: tokens summed per request and rounded to nearest 100 tokens, monthly aggregation for invoices.
- Model weightings: for very large, costly models we may apply a multiplier (e.g., 1.5x) — must be surfaced pre-purchase and in console.
- Transfer between projects: unused free credits do not auto-transfer across accounts; committed credits can be assigned via billing admin.

Discounting and negotiation guardrails (sales playbook):
- List price is canonical. Discounts should be exceptions, logged in the pricing tracker, and approved per tier:
  - Standard promotional discounts (marketing/PLG coupons): up to 25% for < $25k ARR deals, product signoff not required.
  - Sales discounts for Growth->Business: up to 20% with AM approval.
  - Enterprise/Strategic: can negotiate custom combos (commit + lower token prices + Dedicated provisioning) but require AM + RevOps + Legal signoff; always aim for commit terms (12+ months) and minimums that preserve unit economics.
- Swap levers vs. pure discount: prefer adding value rather than deep list price cuts — e.g., enable Dedicated burst windows, longer billing periods, or free training/implementation hours.
- Concessions log: every discount > 10% must have a win-back plan and a renewal pricing cadence recorded.

Pricing language examples (customer-facing bullets):
- "Pay only for the tokens you use — tokens power both text generation and embeddings so you can predict feature costs as usage grows."
- "Committed plans give deeper per-token pricing + reserved capacity for predictable latency and throughput."
- "Teams that need full VPC or on-prem can license Redwood Private with a flat platform fee plus metered usage or a custom committed model."

Objection handling (scripts):
- "Token pricing is confusing" -> "We provide a cost estimator in the console and SDK helpers to approximate tokens per prompt. We also offer trial credits and a sandbox to measure true run-rate before committing."
- "I prefer instance-hours" -> "Instance-hours are great for infra ops budgeting. We offer Dedicated reserve contracts for teams that want instance-level predictability while keeping per-feature metering for engineering/product economics."
- "Can you cap my monthly spend?" -> "Yes — we offer soft caps, hard caps, and commit contracts. For Enterprise we can set contractual spend caps tied to SLAs."

Monitoring and success metrics for pricing maturity:
- PLG funnel conversion from free tokens -> paying customers (30/60/90 day cohort usage).
- Average revenue per 1M tokens by tier and model family.
- Discount frequency and average concession size by ACV band.
- Churn correlation with unit price changes and model migration events.

Open questions & product asks (to align with product/finance):
- Can console surface per-route and per-model token burn estimates in the billing preview? (important for sales demos).
- Need standard model weight multipliers documented and surfaced in API responses.
- Billing: support for monthly vs. quarterly invoicing and automated commit reconciliation.
- A/B of free token bucket sizes (100k vs 250k) — product experiment suggested.

Action items for GTM (next 30 days):
- Finalize list prices and suggested discounts with RevOps.
- Create pricing page copy + calculator that uses token estimates for common patterns (chat session, embeddings index).
- Update sales playbook with concession rules and sample SOW language for committed contracts.
- Product: prioritize console billing preview and model weight metadata endpoints.

Appendix: sample messaging snippets for website and SDR outreach (short):
- Website hero: "Predictable LLM economics: simple token pricing, predictable SLAs, and tools to cut per-token cost."
- SDR cold line: "We help engineering teams reduce per-token inference costs while improving latency — can I share a cost simulation for your current usage?"

End of playbook.
Feedback loop: add comments in this doc or link PRICING-122 for rate-card simulations.
